newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols marginally up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols marginally up in quiet trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were marginally firmer in quiet trading as the underlying bond market consolidated in relatively narrow ranges below Friday's closes, dealers said.
"It's coming in a little bit firm here before tomorrow and Wednesday's auctions (of two- and five-year Treasury notes)," said a trader for a bank affiliate at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for August T-bond futures options was up 0.3 point at 7.9 percent, while September was up 0.1 point at 8.2 percent in late trade.
The bank trader said trading was slow with hardly any deals larger than 500 lots.
The U.S. Treasury is due to auction $15.5 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $11.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.
There was little interest yet to stock up on options ahead of the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
They noted that the Federal Reserve was widely expected to keep interest rates steady at the July FOMC meeting, and this expectation was priced into Fed funds futures prices.

Even gamma players looking for short-term turbulence would probably wait until late in the week, they added. August options, which expire in about four weeks, would have one week less life to maturity and thus higher gamma acceleration, while market makers tend to mark off the weekend time decay by late Friday.
In Eurodollars, volatilities were largely steady, reflecting the mild consolidation in the futures market.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options stood at around 10.0 percent, up 0.1 point on the day.
